title: Agent guardrail
lede: A safety check on every tool call an AI agent makes. Calls that match what the user asked for pass; risky or off-intent calls are blocked or held for approval. Uncertainty fails closed.
if_down: Every tool call is blocked. With no answer the intent match reads as 0, and the guardrail fails closed.

stages.title: Parse the body
stages.text: The input already parses JSON bodies. This stage only parses a body that arrives as a string, so both shapes become the same object before anything else touches it.

stages.title: Stamp the arrival time
stages.text: Adds received_at, the time this node first saw the record. Everything downstream, including the latency figure, is measured from here.

stages.title: Start the latency timer
stages.text: Stores the current time in message metadata. The message itself does not change, so the output below equals the input; the timer is read after Jev answers.

stages.title: Ask Jev
stages.text: One request carries the user's intent and the proposed tool call, with two questions: does the call match the intent, and how risky is it. The answer is merged under `jev`. If Jev cannot be reached, the catch block substitutes an empty answer set, intent match reads as 0, and the call is blocked.

stages.title: Decide where it goes
stages.text: Intent match under 0.3, or a non-safe risk class at 0.7 confidence or more, blocks the call. Any other non-safe risk, or intent match under 0.7, holds it for approval. Only the rest is allowed.

stages.title: Write to a queue
stages.text: Blocked, held and allowed calls are separate JSONL files under data/jev-agent-guardrail/.
